cells.tense: More than one thing is true right now, and you are handling all of it.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Name what this situation is and what it isn't, out loud, to the people it touches — before anyone has to ask you for it.
cells.core:
Many things are true at once for you and none of them gets dropped. You can walk into a messy situation and find the live part of it before the talking is finished, and you don't need the whole argument settled to stand somewhere solid. People bring you the tangled version because you don't make them simplify it first.

What's missing is the saying of it. You settle things internally and leave the table guessing. Say the frame where others can hear it — this is what's in front of everyone, this is what isn't — in your own words, before anyone has to ask you to draw the line. Naming it out loud doesn't thin it. It gives the situation edges that others can hold too.

cells.verb: carrying many true things at once
cells.place: where you sort what deserves your attention

cells.tense: Readings are piling up in advance of anything that has actually happened yet.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Choose the heading you want and hold it for three days — no surveying the alternatives, no reviewing whether a different pick was wiser.
cells.core:
Every possible version of what's coming is being kept open and defended with good reasons, and the stack gets taller before anything occurs. Inside, this reads as caution. Outside, the people near you watch you prepare for eight outcomes and commit to none.

The plenty is being used to avoid a heading. What's needed isn't another reading of the field. Take one direction — the wanted one, not the most defensible one — and follow it for three days. No checking on the roads not taken. Knowing what matters only sharpens when you're moving one way; from a survey, it can't tell.

cells.tense: You were at a threshold that had already opened, and you stayed where you were.
cells.act: meet someone in the middle and go on together
cells.ask: Bring the unfinished thing to one person — say the rough half, hear what they bring, and walk on with whatever the two of you end up making.
cells.core:
Something is waiting past a step you've taken, and you haven't crossed. Your sense of what matters is still there; it just isn't in motion, parked behind a wait that has turned into the whole posture. The decision got put off, and the putting-off has gone on longer than the deciding would have.

Don't force yourself into the blank. Hand the half-made thing to one person and stand in it with them — the untidy version, out loud, and whatever they add to it. Two lines of work running as one gets this off the mark. The next solid step shows up from the meeting, not from waiting until it's certain.

cells.tense: You can feel what's fair in this, and you're attributing the call to someone else.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Settle the small debt you owe — the one nobody else is tracking — and don't mention to anybody that you did it.
cells.core:
A private, accurate read of what's fair sits in you about a situation that's still open, and that read keeps getting credited to the room. You did the weighing. You talk as though the balance arrived by itself, and the people in it have nothing to correct you with.

Start smaller than the situation. Somewhere in it there's an unmarked debt — a correction, a payment, a thing to put back — and it's clear to you and it's clear to nobody else. Settle it quietly, by your own hand, and keep it unannounced. The sense that named it is yours, and acting on it without witness is how it stops being the room's.
cells.sheetLine: You weigh what's fair and credit the room for it.
